we have found a small deletion that interferes with genotyping for the C9orf72 expansion mutation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C9orf72 expansion is not detectable in 25% of expansion-positive cases using the standard repeat-primed PCR method, and that the use of alternative methods to identify the mutation in this gene is recommended.
the repeat-primed PCR assay is a highly reliable test, with a false-negative rate of approximately 1 in 40.
the repeat expansion mutation is not detectable by repeat-primed PCR in 2% of the C9orf72 expansion carriers, and that this is due to a small deletion in the repeat expansion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deletion is not the cause of FTLD but is an important confounding factor in the detection of expansion mutations in C9orf072.
the C9orf72 repeat expansion mutation can be missed in up to 25% of patients using standard genotyping methods.

the deletion in C9ORF72 is a common cause of C9orf72 expansion-negative frontotemporal lobe dementia and that this deletion is a common cause for false-negative C9orf72 repeat primed polymerase chain reactions.

a small deletion in C10orf72 can hide a proportion of expansion mutation carriers in FTLD.
